text.p: These are the leading stories in the Algerian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Security forces kill "terrorist gang" in Algiers.
- Political parties step up preparations for the parliamentary elections on June 5.
- Four new newspapers, Demain l'Algerie, Al Alam, La Nouvelle Republique and Saout al Ahrar, to appear soon in Algeria.
- Only seven political parties out of more than 60 were not affected by the party law banning politicians from using Islam or regional differences in their platforms to compete for power.
- Security forces kill 12 "terrorists" in Algiers and 25 in Sour el Ghozlane, south of Algiers.
- Foreign Minister Ahmed Attaf to address European Union parliament on cooperation in the Mediterranean area.
- Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia may be a candidate in the elections as well as Information and Culture Minister Mihoub Mihoubi and President Liamine Zeroual's adviser Mokdad Sifi.
- Security forces kill 12 "terrorits" near Algiers Djebel Koukou area and three others in Bab Ali, south of Algiers.
- Salah Boubnider, a former nationalist fighter, is tipped to head an independent committee to supervise the elections.
